title: Orthogonal localization triangle for a small family in a Grothendieck derived category
statement: Fix a universe $U$ for Hom sets and small indexing sets [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal B$ be Grothendieck abelian relative to $U$ [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], and let $D(\mathcal B)$ be its ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $I\in U$ and let $P_i\in D(\mathcal B)$ for $i\in I$. Define $\mathcal L$ to be the smallest full replete triangulated subcategory [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory] containing all $P_i$ and closed under $U$-small coproducts computed in $D(\mathcal B)$. For every $Y\in D(\mathcal B)$ there is a distinguished triangle $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$ in $D(\mathcal B)$ with $X\in\mathcal L$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal B)}(W,Z)=0$ for every $W\in\mathcal L$.

source.place: Lemma A.1, proof: the localizing hull of a set in a well-generated ambient category is well generated, its inclusion has a right adjoint, and the orthogonal triangle exists; Remark A.2 specializes the ambient category to D(B) Hall--Neeman--Rydh, arXiv:1405.1888, Appendix A. No Stacks tag states this input; archive WANTED, online source read.

proof.text: Put $T=D(\mathcal B)$. The functorial K-injective resolution theorem applies to the Grothendieck category $\mathcal B$; the derived local-smallness statement therefore gives $U$-small Hom groups in $T$. The derived coproduct theorem gives all $U$-small coproducts. Since $\mathcal L$ is full, replete, triangulated and closed under those ambient coproducts, it inherits the triangulation and these same coproducts. In particular it has countable coproducts, so its idempotents split. These are precisely the size, triangulation, coproduct and idempotent hypotheses needed below.

source.place: Appendix A, Lemma A.1 proof and Remark A.2; representing the restricted Hom functor gives the coreflection used there. Brown inputs supplied by existing solution-set nodes.

proof.text: Fix $Y\in T$ and define $H:\mathcal L^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Ab}_U$ by $H(W)=\operatorname{Hom}_T(W,Y)$, with $H(f)(a)=a\circ f$. It is additive. The Hom-out-of-a-triangle exactness lemma, applied to all rotations and shifts of a distinguished triangle in $\mathcal L$, gives its long exact cohomological sequence; consecutive maps compose to zero by the Hom-into-triangle lemma on those rotations. For a $U$-small family $(W_j)$, restriction to the coprojections identifies $H(\coprod_jW_j)$ with $\prod_jH(W_j)$: the inverse sends $(a_j)$ to the unique map from the coproduct restricting to every $a_j$. Hence $H$ carries these coproducts to products.

source.place: Appendix A, Lemma A.1 proof and Remark A.2; representing the restricted Hom functor gives the coreflection used there. Brown inputs supplied by existing solution-set nodes.

proof.text: The family $(P_i)_{i\in I}$ is $U$-small and $\mathcal L$ is its minimal replete triangulated coproduct-closed hull. Apply the set-generated derived solution-set theorem to this family and to $H$ of step 2. It supplies a $U$-small family $(B_j,b_j\in H(B_j))$ through which every element of every $H(W)$ pulls back. The cohomological solution-set representability theorem now applies to $\mathcal L$, using step 1 for split idempotents and the common Hom universe and step 2 for cohomologicality and coproducts-to-products. Obtain $X\in\mathcal L$ and natural bijections $\theta_W:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal L}(W,X)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_T(W,Y)$.

source.place: Appendix A, Lemma A.1 proof and Remark A.2; representing the restricted Hom functor gives the coreflection used there. Brown inputs supplied by existing solution-set nodes.

proof.text: Set $\epsilon=\theta_X(1_X):X\to Y$. For every $W\in\mathcal L$ and $f:W\to X$, naturality at $f$ gives $\theta_W(f)=\epsilon\circ f$. Fullness of $\mathcal L$ identifies its Hom groups with those of $T$, so postcomposition with $\epsilon$ is bijective on $\operatorname{Hom}_T(W,-)$. Since $W[-1]\in\mathcal L$, shifting the same bijection for $W[-1]$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_T(W,X[1])\to\operatorname{Hom}_T(W,Y[1])$ induced by $\epsilon[1]$.

source.place: Appendix A, Lemma A.1 proof and Remark A.2; representing the restricted Hom functor gives the coreflection used there. Brown inputs supplied by existing solution-set nodes.

proof.text: Complete $\epsilon$ to a distinguished triangle $X\xrightarrow{\epsilon}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z\xrightarrow{d}X[1]$ by TR1. Fix $W\in\mathcal L$ and $a:W\to Z$. Consecutive composites in the rotated triangles are zero, so $\epsilon[1]\circ d\circ a=0$. Injectivity of postcomposition with $\epsilon[1]$ from step 4 forces $d\circ a=0$. Apply Hom exactness at $Z$ (clause (ii) for the rotated triangle) to write $a=g\circ b$ for $b:W\to Y$. By surjectivity in step 4 write $b=\epsilon\circ c$. Thus $a=g\circ\epsilon\circ c=0$. This proves $\operatorname{Hom}_T(W,Z)=0$ for every $W\in\mathcal L$; together with $X\in\mathcal L$ it is the required triangle.
